cta_long: Quiz in bio: which AI business fits how you work.

days.line: Life gets a lot simpler when you stop breaking promises to yourself.

You don't need another idea.
You need to finish the last one you were excited about.

You were never lazy.
You were unscheduled.
days.question: What's one thing you keep meaning to put on the calendar?
variants: Lazy was never the problem. No schedule was.

days.line:
Starting is your superpower.
Finishing is the skill.
Practice the skill.
days.question: What's the last thing you started and actually finished?

days.line:
The business doesn't pay for what you started this week.
It pays for what you shipped.
days.question: What's one thing you can ship this week, even if it's small?
variants: Nobody pays for started. They pay for shipped.

days.line:
Old way: wait until you feel focused.
New way: start for 10 minutes and let focus catch up.
days.question: What's the task you've been waiting to feel ready for?

days.line:
One week in. Seven posts.
None felt ready. All of them went out.
days.question: What are you shipping this week, ready or not?
days.condition: Post only if Days 1-7 all went out. If one was missed, swap with Day 8 and rewrite the count before posting.

days.line:
Your head is a terrible filing cabinet.
Paper remembers so you can build.
days.question: Paper, notes app, or voice memos? Where do your ideas go?

days.line:
AI won't replace the entrepreneur.
It replaces the excuse "I don't have a team."
days.question: What's the first job you'd hand off if you had a team?
variants: AI didn't replace you. It replaced your best excuse.
"I don't have a team" stopped being a reason.

days.line:
Busy is easy.
Done is rare.
Be rare.
days.question: What's one thing you got done today? Not worked on. Done.
variants: Anyone can be busy. Be done.
Busy is a feeling. Done is a fact.

days.line:
Every unfinished project charges you rent in your head.
Finish one. Evict the noise.
days.question: Which unfinished project is living rent-free in your head right now?
variants: Unfinished projects don't sit quietly. They charge rent.
Half-done projects are the loudest thing in your head.

days.line:
Posting daily beats building in secret.
Nobody buys what they never saw.
days.question: What have you been building in secret?

days.line:
Mood decides if you feel like it.
The plan decides if you do it.
days.question: What's one thing you'll do tomorrow whether you feel like it or not?

days.line:
Give AI the boring jobs.
Keep the decisions.
days.question: What's the most boring task in your business?

days.line:
Two weeks of posts with no link.
Today I'm showing what I'm building.
days.question: What kind of business are you building? One word.
days.condition: Website on hold since Oct 23, so this line no longer fits. Zucc and Claude bring a replacement founder line to the Nov 4 pre-post for Wil's OK.

days.line:
Old way: another app, another system, another reset.
New way: one list, one priority, one finish.
days.question: How many to-do apps have you tried? Be honest.

days.line:
Ideas are cheap for people like us.
Follow-through is the flex.
days.question: How many ideas are sitting in your notes app right now?

days.line:
Discipline for a fast brain isn't working harder.
It's making the list shorter.
days.question: What can come off your list today?

days.line:
You don't need ten AI tools.
You need one set up for your business.
days.question: How many AI tools are you paying for right now?

days.line:
Strategy isn't what you add.
It's what you refuse.
days.question: What's one thing you said no to this month?

days.line:
Motivation gets you a new project.
A schedule gets you a finished one.
days.question: What's on your calendar this week that used to be "someday"?
variants: Motivation starts projects. Schedules finish them.
Feelings start things. Calendars finish them.

days.line:
AI doesn't fix a messy business.
It makes the mess faster.
days.question: What's one process you'd clean up before handing it to AI?

days.line:
Nobody is coming to organize your ideas for you.
Write them down, pick one, finish it.
That's the whole system.
days.question: Which idea are you picking? Put it in the comments to make it real.
variants: Write it down. Pick one. Finish it. That's the whole system.
days.note: Original is 19 words, over the 15-word house max. The variant is the tight version; Wil's pick.

days.line:
If you can't be bad at it in public,
you can't get good at it.
days.question: What are you willing to be bad at in public this month?

days.line:
Talent is a head start.
Reps are the race.
days.question: What are you counting reps on right now?

days.line:
AI can't choose your one thing.
It can help you finish it.
days.question: What's your one thing this week?

days.line:
You don't need a big audience.
You need the right hundred people.
days.question: Describe your right hundred people in five words.

days.line:
Do it once by hand.
Write it down.
Then hand it to AI.
days.question: What's a task you've done by hand enough times to write down?

days.line:
One offer, sold well,
beats five offers explained badly.
days.question: If you could only sell one thing, what would it be?

days.line:
Thirty days ago I promised myself one post a day.
Promise kept.
days.question: What promise to yourself are you keeping this month?
days.condition: Callback to Day 1. Post only if all 30 went out. If not, use: "Thirty days in. I missed [N]. I didn't quit. That's the whole trick."
